chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd al-Ash'ari, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the child, can he be breastfed for more than two years? So he said: 'Two years'. I said, 'So if it is increased upon the two years, is there anything upon its parents from that?' He said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a child is breastfed for more than two years?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) confirms the two-year standard for breastfeeding while clarifying that exceeding this duration incurs no religious penalty (*la*), indicating flexibility in the practice. This ruling aligns with the Quranic baseline but reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that the two-year period is a recommended norm rather than a strict limit, allowing for extended nursing based on mutual agreement and the child's needs.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sa’ad Bin Al Ashary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the child, can he be breastfed for more than two years?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Two years’. I said, ‘So if is increased upon the two years, is there anything upon its parents from that?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d al-Ash‘ariy who has said the following: “I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a child; if he can be breastfed for more than two years.
He (the Imam) said, ‘It is two years.’ I then asked, ‘If the child is breastfed for more than two years do parents owe anything?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, they do not owe anything.
